Plot snapshots¶

wvt saves the plots as PNG files, as they show on the screen. Use the snapshots in reports or to compare two recordings.

Save snapshots¶

  1. Set the plots as you want them in the snapshot.

  2. Click Snapshot… at the bottom left of the window, or select File → Save plot snapshots….

  3. In the Save plot snapshots window, tick the plots to save. All and None tick all the plots or no plots.

  4. Make sure that the Folder is correct. The default is ~/wvt-recordings/. wvt makes the folder if it does not exist.

  5. Click Export.

The window closes, and wvt saves one PNG file for each plot. The status bar shows the result. To close the window without a save, click Cancel.

wvt does not replace a snapshot file. If a different wvt window uses the same number at the same time, wvt uses the next number.

Plots¶

Plot

Mode

Contents

Overview strip

File

The power over the full file or segment, with the view box

Spectrum

File, Device

The spectrum of the view, or the live spectrum

Waterfall

File, Device

The waterfall with its color bar

I / Q, AM, FM, PM

File

The time plot with its header (name, readout)

  • A plot that is not on the screen is not available. For example, a hidden time plot, or the time plots in Device mode.

  • The time plots scroll. If a time plot is only partly on the screen, the window shows partly hidden. wvt then saves only the part on the screen. To save all of the plot, scroll the plots or set a smaller plot height in the channel options.

File names¶

The file name is <recording>_capture_<plot>_<n>.png, for example cap_915MHz_capture_waterfall_3.png.

  • <recording> is the name of the open recording without its folder and extension. In Device mode, it is live.

  • <plot> is overview, spectrum, waterfall, iq, am, fm or pm.

  • <n> is the first number that no snapshot of this recording in the folder uses. All the files of one export have the same number. Thus wvt does not write over a previous snapshot.

The window shows the names before you export.

Image quality¶

  • The PNG files have no loss. Each pixel is the same as on the screen.

  • The image size is the size of the plot on the screen. For larger images, make the window or the plot larger, or start wvt with a larger --scale.

  • The pointer crosshair and tooltips are not in the snapshots.

How it works¶

Each plot records its screen rectangle on each frame. When you click Export, wvt hides the pointer for two frames, so that no crosshair or tooltip shows. After the next frame is drawn, wvt reads the frame (from OpenGL or the software renderer) and cuts out each plot. The PNG encoder is stb_image_write in third_party/stb/. The self-check build/snapshot_check tests the file names, the numbering, the crop and the PNG files.

For the design, refer to the snapshot design record.
